places.name: Barcelona Pavilion
places.note: Mies van der Rohe's 1929 pavilion, rebuilt in 1986: onyx, travertine, still water and free-standing planes. Go early, when it is nearly empty.

places.name: Fundació Joan Miró
places.note: Sert's white museum for his friend, top-lit and terraced into the hill. The roof garden looks across the whole city.

places.name: Casa Vicens
places.note: Gaudí's first house, tiled with marigolds, all Moorish exuberance. Far quieter than his later famous works.

places.name: Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau
places.address: Carrer de Sant Antoni Maria Claret 167
places.note: Domènech i Montaner's hospital city: tiled pavilions in gardens, linked by underground tunnels. Medicine as architecture.

places.name: Palau de la Música Catalana
places.note: A concert hall of glass, mosaic and sculpture, under an inverted stained-glass dome. Better at a concert than on a tour.

places.name: Mercat de Santa Caterina
places.note: Miralles Tagliabue's undulating roof of coloured tiles, a pixelated fruit stall over an old market. Shop for lunch underneath.

places.name: Fundació Antoni Tàpies
places.note: Tàpies's foundation in an early Domènech building, crowned with a cloud of tangled wire. Tough, material, quiet art.

places.name: Museu del Disseny
places.note: A cantilevered block nicknamed 'the stapler', holding Barcelona's design collections. Chairs, posters, fashion.

places.name: La Fábrica
places.note: Bofill's converted cement works, his home and studio: silos, cypresses, cathedral volumes. Worth the trip out of town; tours are occasional.

places.name: El Xampanyet
places.note: A tiled cava bar in the same family for generations. House cava, anchovies, elbows at the counter.

places.name: Bar Cañete
places.note: A long counter and fast, precise tapas cooked in front of you. Sit at the bar, not the tables.
